result:
Done. All acceptance criteria pass.

**Files**
- `src/types.ts` - Todo + input types
- `src/store.ts` - `TodoStore`, Map-backed, in-memory
- `src/validation.ts` - title/completed/query rules, returns `{ok}` result union
- `src/app.ts` - Express 5 routes + JSON error handler
- `src/server.ts` - listens port 3000 (`PORT` env override)
- `src/app.test.ts` - 21 tests, `node:test`, real HTTP on ephemeral port
- `README.md`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore`

**Verified**
- clean `npm install` then `npm test`: 21 pass, 0 fail
- `tsc --noEmit` strict (plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`): 0 errors
- live curl run of every endpoint: 201 create, 400 blank title, 400 201-char title, filter true/false, 200 patch, 204 delete, 404 missing id, `{"error":"..."}` body shape everywhere

**Deps**: express only. Dev: typescript, @types/node, @types/express. No supertest - tests use built-in `fetch`.

**One note on port 3000**: your ekoa Next dev server holds `127.0.0.1:3000`. My server still binds 3000 (wildcard, SO_REUSEADDR) and logs listening, but curl to `localhost:3000` reaches next-server, not mine. So functional curl pass ran on `PORT=3100`. Default port code is plain `3000`; nothing to fix, just port conflict on this box.

Test runner choice: build to `dist/` then `node --test dist/*.test.js`. Node 20 cannot strip TS types, so this avoids adding ts-node/tsx, and `npm test` typechecks as side effect.
